title: FAA UAP record 237UAP00625
what_is_it: FAA Washington Operations Center incident notification documenting a UAP sighting reported by a commercial airline crew.
core_summary: On 14 April 2024, the crew of Delta Air Lines flight 1706 (a Boeing 717-200) flying from Atlanta to Charlotte reported observing an unidentified anomalous phenomenon at flight level 234 (approximately 23,400 feet) near the PHIIL waypoint in the vicinity of Rutledge, Georgia. No evasive action was taken by the aircraft, and no law-enforcement notification was reported.

public_headline: Delta crew reported unidentified object at 23,400 feet over Georgia
public_tldr: This FAA operations-centre log records that the crew of Delta Air Lines flight 1706, a Boeing 717-200, reported seeing an unidentified anomalous phenomenon while flying at roughly 23,400 feet near Rutledge, Georgia on 14 April 2024. No evasive action was taken and no law-enforcement notification was filed.
public_narrative:
This document is a preliminary incident notification from the FAA's Washington Operations Center (WOC). It logs a report relayed from the Eastern Regional Operations Center (E-ROC) about a UAP — unidentified anomalous phenomenon — sighted by a commercial airline crew.

On 14 April 2024 at approximately 7:40 a.m. Eastern time, the crew of Delta Air Lines flight 1706, operating a Boeing 717-200 on the Atlanta-to-Charlotte route, reported observing a UAP at flight level 234 — roughly 23,400 feet. The sighting occurred near an aviation waypoint called PHIIL, in the vicinity of Rutledge, Georgia (coordinates 33.63°N, 83.61°W).

The log notes that no evasive action was taken by the aircraft and that no law-enforcement notification was reported. There is no description of the object's shape, size, movement, or behaviour in the document.

The record is a short operational log entry, not a full investigation report. It contains no radar data, sensor evidence, photographs, or follow-up findings. It simply confirms that the crew made the report and that it was logged through standard FAA channels.
public_caveats: This is a preliminary operations-centre log, not a completed investigation — it records that a report was made, nothing more.
No corroborating evidence is included: no radar data, no sensor readings, no photographs, and no follow-up investigation results.
The document does not describe what the crew saw — only that they reported a UAP. There is no detail on the object's appearance or behaviour.
The filing metadata lists the incident year as 2023, but the document itself clearly dates the event to 14 April 2024 — this appears to be a metadata discrepancy.
The source is a single crew report relayed through FAA channels; no independent witness or instrument confirmation is present in this record.
